observation.body: The public chat handler fails closed because the host cannot attest its payload; verified user-context polling is the only active observer: {enabled}, up to 256 records every {seconds} seconds. Poll records contain a character route but no person or conversation ID, so user scope is character-only and may mix people sharing a character; conversation scope stops learning from those records. Routes expire after five minutes. Queuing has no delivery acknowledgement, and the host may silently drop it or reroute a target that disappears.

option.scope_conversation: Per user and conversation (polling stops without an ID)
option.scope_user: Per user (polling falls back to character)

profile.create_help: The entered name only derives and selects a local pseudonymous profile; it never validates or establishes guidance routing. Management injection requires real chat from that catgirl seen in this process within the last five minutes. It is not a user name and is omitted from safe exports.

timing.body: Verified user-context polling normally runs every two seconds and checks at most 256 records per pass, so guidance generally starts on a later turn. The public chat handler rejects unverified calls. Panel creation never validates routing; management injection requires a real route observed within five minutes. Salted restart fingerprints detect collisions only and do not restore routes. The host provides neither strict target-only routing nor delivery acknowledgement, so a queue call may be silently lost or rerouted. Consumed read guidance may remain in conversation history; counters represent queue attempts only.
